Results and Discussion Effect of Buffer Species on FLuc mRNA-LNP Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) To study the effect of storage buffer species on mRNA-LNP CQAs ( i.e. , hydrodynamic diameter, encapsulation efficiency, and transfection efficiency), a consistent LNP formulation was exchanged into three storage buffers: Tris (p K a ≈ 8.1), histidine (p K a ≈ 6.0) and citrate (p K a ≈ 4.8) ( Figure b). Formulations using LP-01, MC3 and SM-102 ionizable lipids were compared for all three buffers at 50 mM buffer, 45 mM NaCl and 5 wt % sucrose. The mRNA-LNPs formulated in Tris and histidine buffers achieved the target pH of 7.4, while those in citrate buffer displayed a modestly reduced pH of 6.9. At these measured pH values, all formulations exhibited high encapsulation efficiency (89–94%), as measured by the RiboGreen assay. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) and cryo-TEM revealed particle sizes in the range of 60–120 nm ( Figure S1 ). Cryo-TEM also showed that particles were generally spherical and monodisperse, although histidine-buffered LNPs displayed greater size heterogeneity ( Figures S1a and S2 ). Despite comparable external morphologies, the transfection efficiency in HepG2 cells varied markedly, with fresh citrate-buffered mRNA-LNPs demonstrating the highest performance in all three studied ionizable lipids ( Figure c). For instance, SM-102 mRNA-LNPs in citrate storage buffers exhibited 151% higher transfection efficiency compared to the same nanoparticles in Tris storage buffers. These results are consistent with previous reports, which demonstrated higher EE values in PEGylated nano-systems when compared to their non-PEGylated alternatives [ 67 ]. The slightly reduced DL in the PEGylated formulation can be explained by the additional mass contributed by DSPE-PEG 2000 , which increases the overall weight of the nanocarrier and reduces the proportion of drug relative to total nanoparticle mass. Surface morphology by HRTEM HRTEM analysis confirmed that optimized DPZ-PEGylated NLCs exhibited a well-defined spherical morphology with high uniformity in size and shape, smooth surfaces, and no visible aggregation, all indicative of good physical stability (Fig. 6 A). The optimized DPZ-PEGylated NLCs displayed an average PS of approximately 128.75 nm, which was consistent with the DLS measurement, validating agreement between microscopic and light-scattering techniques. The micrographs also revealed a distinct core–shell structure, where the dense core represented the lipid matrix encapsulating DPZ and the lighter outer shell corresponded to the DSPE-PEG 2000 coating, confirming successful PEGylation of the nanoparticle surface. In contrast, uncoated NLCs (Fig. 6 B) showed a slightly larger average PS of ~ 158.37 nm, with less distinct surface boundaries and a more irregular texture. The absence of the DSPE PEG 2000 layer likely contributed to this increased size variation and exposed the lipid matrix directly, making the uncoated particles more prone to aggregation or fusion during storage [ 68 ].
